footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $10,172M; this page starts from gross revenue of $14,144M so the $3,972M of client incentives shows as a cost.
oneTimers: A litigation provision of $615M sits in operating expenses — the special item for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case and other legal matters; Visa excludes it from non-GAAP results.

Also excluded from non-GAAP results: $73M of amortization of acquired intangible assets and acquisition-related costs, and $35M of net losses on equity investments. Non-GAAP net income was $5.8B ($2.98 per share).
otherDetail: Investment income and other gains of $195M, less $39M of interest expense — net +$156M.

segments.name: Service revenue
segments.note: Fees from banks for using the Visa brand and network on cards — based on the prior quarter's payments volume.

segments.name: Data processing revenue
segments.note: Fees for clearing and processing each transaction — processed transactions grew 10%.

segments.name: International transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees when a card is used outside its home country — cross-border volume rose 12% in nominal terms.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Value-added services — fraud tools, data and consulting for banks and merchants.

takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 14% to $10.2B — data processing +15%, international transactions +14%, service revenue +9% and other revenue +32%. Payments volume grew 9% and processed transactions 10%.
takeaways.title: Volume growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: Non-GAAP EPS was $2.98, up 23%, and non-GAAP net income $5.8B, up 19%. GAAP EPS rose 12% to $2.69 because of the legal charge below.
takeaways.title: Underlying EPS rose 23%

takeaways.text: The litigation provision was $615M — mostly the special item for the interchange MDL case and other legal matters, vs just $10M a year ago. It pushed GAAP operating expenses up 35%; excluding such items, they rose 13%.
takeaways.title: The legal bill spiked again

verdict: Visa's net revenue rose 14% to $10.2B as payments volume grew 9% and cross-border volume 12% — but a $615M litigation provision held GAAP profit growth to 8% ($5.3B), even as underlying EPS rose 23%.
